claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child. His name is Alex and he's 5 years old. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, are you paying at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount (or more) towards his upkeep, such as for food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's actually part of the issue. Alex's other parent and I are both responsible for him, but we can't agree on who should claim the Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important situation to understand.

**Can you tell me more about the living arrangements? Specifically:**
- **Do you and Alex's other parent live together, or do you live separately?**
- **If you live separately, does Alex live primarily with you, or does he spend time living with both of you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We live separately, and Alex lives with me primarily - he's at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to understand the situation.

Just to clarify one more thing:

**Has Alex's other parent already submitted a claim for Child Benefit for Alex, or are they just saying they want to claim it?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: They're saying they want to claim it, but we just can't agree on who should be the one to actually claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or living with someone else for any extended period of time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of that. Alex lives at home with me full-time.

## Assessment Complete

**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ Alex is 5 years old (under 16) - meets the age requirement  
✓ You live in the UK  
✓ Alex lives with you primarily - which means you are responsible for him  

**Important information about your situation:**

Since you and Alex's other parent cannot agree on who should claim, here's what you need to know:

- **Only one person can receive Child Benefit for Alex** - two people cannot both get it for the same child
- **You are eligible to submit a claim** since Alex lives with you primarily
- If both you and the other parent submit separate claims, HMRC will decide who receives the Child Benefit
- The fact that Alex lives primarily with you supports your claim

**What to do next:**

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. If you and the other parent are unable to agree between yourselves who should claim, and both of you submit claims, HMRC will make the final decision based on the circumstances.

**One additional thing to be aware of:** If either you or your partner has an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.
